prompt.context: Your client is FlashPro Inc., a San Francisco based technology company that develops and sells wearable and mountable action cameras. FlashPro's CEO believes that the company's growth has stagnated and has hired your firm to remedy that issue.
prompt.question: FlashPro's growth has stagnated. Diagnose the situation and recommend how the company can achieve growth.

clarifying_info.a: The company is public. It sells its products in the US and internationally.
Their main product is CamPro, a mounted camera mainly used when playing action sports. It has also recently started being used in other recreational activities.

clarifying_info.q: Does FlashPro manufacture its own products?
clarifying_info.a: FlashPro does not manufacture its products; it contracts with manufacturers in China.

clarifying_info.q: How does FlashPro sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: FlashPro sells its products through 3 channels: Distributors, Retail, and FlashPro's Website.

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive landscape like?
clarifying_info.a: The industry is highly competitive and customers are very loyal to each brand.
Gross margin has remained steady at 50%.

clarifying_info.q: What is the US vs. international revenue split?
clarifying_info.a: Over the last 5 years, 60% of camera sales have come from the US. The split is expected to be similar in 2018.

exhibits.title: Action Camera Potential Market in the US
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the US action camera addressable market (in thousands of customers) from 2014 to 2020 (2014A-2017A actuals, 2018E-2020E estimates).

exhibits.title: Action Camera Market Penetration in the US
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of the US addressable market that has already purchased an action camera, from 2014 to 2020 (actuals and estimates).

exhibits.title: 2016 Action Camera Market Share Distribution
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing market share among action camera brands. Market share distribution is the same in the US and worldwide and has remained steady for the last 5 years. FlashPro is the only company offering wearables.

exhibits.title: Potential New Country Markets
exhibits.shows: A table comparing four candidate countries (Argentina, Japan, Australia, Sweden) across current camera market size, FlashPro's expected Year 1 market share, expected annual growth over 3 years, and sales channel distribution (Distributors, Retail, FlashPro's Website). Dollar amounts in thousands.

data.note: After Year 3, expected market annual growth for all countries is 5%

framework: Market Analysis: Competitors, customers, substitutes, suppliers — assess competitive dynamics and customer loyalty
Profitability Tree: Break down revenue (volume x price) and costs (COGS, R&D, G&A, Sales & Marketing) to identify where growth is constrained
Revenue Growth Levers: Marketing Mix (4Ps — product attributes, sales channels, price, advertising), new markets (product line expansion, new geographies), organic vs. inorganic (M&A)
Cost Structure: Gross margin components and operating cost efficiency

questions.prompt: Question 1: What is FlashPro's expected Gross Profit for 2018? (Use Exhibits 1, 2, and 3 along with clarifying info)
questions.guidance: Candidate must build revenue from the addressable market data (Exhibit 1), apply penetration rate (Exhibit 2) and FlashPro's market share (Exhibit 3), then use camera price and gross margin to arrive at gross profit. Should recognize that all amounts are in thousands and that international revenue is derived from the US/international split.

math.setup: All amounts in thousands. Camera price = $250. Gross margin = 50%. US share of revenue = 60%, International = 40%.
steps: US camera units sold (implied) = 16,000 × 85% × 30% — but since price is per unit and amounts are in thousands, compute US revenue directly: 16,000 × 85% × 30% × $250 = $1,020,000 (thousands)

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are FlashPro's revenue growth prospects keeping everything constant, and what other alternatives could boost the top line?
questions.guidance: Candidate should draw on Exhibits 1-3 to identify organic US growth constraints: the US market is growing slowly (16,000 to 16,700 over 3 years) and penetration is high (85% in 2018 rising to 95% by 2020), leaving little room for US volume growth. Market share has been steady for 5 years so share gains are difficult. A strong candidate provides an organized framework: Marketing Mix (4Ps: product attributes, new features, additional sales channels, pricing strategy, advertising/promotion); New Markets (product line expansion — e.g., new camera categories, software; new geographies); Organic growth (R&D, internal development); Inorganic growth (M&A, partnerships).

questions.prompt: Question 3: From an economic perspective, which country is most attractive for FlashPro to enter, and what considerations should FlashPro weigh before entering? (Use Exhibit 4)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate Year 3 revenues for each country and compare. An excellent candidate notes the sales channel distribution matters because FlashPro's Website channel carries higher margins (no intermediary), so a higher website mix is more profitable. Argentina wins on both Year 3 revenue and sales channel mix (50% website vs. 10% for Japan and Sweden). Candidate should also list structured pre-entry considerations: customer habits and brand loyalty, local competition, regulation, country economic and geopolitical stability, logistics and supply chain, pricing strategy.

math.setup: Year 3 revenue = (Current market size × Year 1 market share) × (1 + annual growth)^3. Growth applied to the current-year revenue base each period. All amounts in thousands.
steps: Argentina: Base = $2,500 × 35% = $875; Year 1 = $875; Year 2 = $875 × 1.10 = $962.5; Year 3 = $962.5 × 1.10 = $1,058.75 ≈ $1,058.75 (casebook rounds to ~$1,165 applying growth to Year 0 base and compounding: $2,500 × 35% = $875 Year 1; Year 3 = $875 × (1.10)^2 ≈ $1,058.75; casebook answer = $1,165 suggesting Year 1 already reflects a growth step: $2,500 × 1.10 × 35% = $962.5 Year 1; Year 3 = $962.5 × (1.10)^2 ≈ $1,165)
Ranking by Year 3 revenue: Argentina $1,165 > Japan $1,013 > Sweden $951 > Australia $932
math.answer: Argentina is the most attractive market with Year 3 revenue of ~$1,165 thousand, and its 50% website channel share provides higher margins than the other candidates.

brainstorming.prompt: What alternatives could help FlashPro boost its top line revenue?

categories.name: Marketing Mix (4Ps)
ideas: Introduce new product features or accessories (e.g., improved stabilization, live streaming)
Add or optimize sales channels (e.g., direct-to-consumer, e-commerce partnerships)
Adjust pricing strategy (e.g., premium line, entry-level model)
Increase advertising spend and brand awareness campaigns
Launch promotions and bundles targeting new user segments

categories.name: New Markets — Product Line Expansion
ideas: Develop software or subscription services (e.g., cloud storage, editing tools)
Launch a consumer-grade dash-cam or security camera
Expand wearable product line (FlashPro is the only wearable player — leverage this differentiation)
Target new recreational use cases beyond action sports (e.g., travel vlogging, pet cameras)

categories.name: New Markets — Geographies
ideas: Enter high-growth international markets (Argentina, Australia, Japan, Sweden per Exhibit 4)
Prioritize markets with lower penetration and less entrenched competition
Partner with local distributors to accelerate entry

categories.name: Organic Growth
ideas: Invest in R&D for next-generation camera technology
Build out FlashPro's website as a higher-margin direct channel
Develop a loyalty/community program to improve customer retention

categories.name: Inorganic Growth (M&A / Partnerships)
ideas: Acquire a complementary technology company (e.g., software, AI, optics)
Form strategic partnerships with sports brands or media companies

recommendation: Given the highly competitive US landscape and limited domestic market growth, FlashPro should pursue a geographic expansion strategy to achieve meaningful top-line growth.

Argentina is the most attractive entry market: it offers the highest expected Year 3 revenue (~$1,165 thousand), the most favorable sales channel mix (50% through FlashPro's website, which carries higher margins due to no intermediary), and a solid Year 1 market share assumption of 35%.
risks: Entry cost and capital requirements were not factored into the analysis — actual profitability may differ once marketing, logistics, and localization costs are included.
The Year 1 market share assumption of 35% in Argentina may be aggressive given that customers are loyal to existing brands and FlashPro has no prior presence there.
Did not account for competitive responses from established local players or other global brands entering the same markets.
Currency and geopolitical risk in Argentina (economic volatility) could affect actual returns.
next_steps: Conduct deeper due diligence on the Argentinian market: customer habits, local competition, regulatory environment, and economic stability.
Assess the internal capabilities (supply chain, local partnerships, marketing) needed to execute the expansion.
Plan a market entry strategy including advertising, sales channel setup, pricing, and promotional campaigns tailored to Argentinian consumers.
Evaluate whether to enter additional markets (Australia, Japan, Sweden) sequentially or in parallel once Argentina entry is underway.
